     "question": "When colorectal cancer has extrahepatic disease that is treated or completely treatable, when should liver resection be offered?",
     "kind": "clinical",
     "status": "Proposed · OPEN proposal",
     "where": [],
     "proposal": "Treated or completely treatable extrahepatic disease is not an absolute contraindication to curative-intent liver resection, but complete clearance of every site is mandatory and benefit depends on the site. Lung disease has the best outcome; nodal disease does poorly (pooled 5-year survival about 15%), worst beyond the hepatic pedicle; limited peritoneal disease belongs to expert CRS/HIPEC centres. Any extrahepatic disease ends transplant intent (CRLM-B5).",

      "Counsel: recurrence about 90%; 10-year disease-free survival about 3% after resection with extrahepatic disease."

     "set": "roadmap",
     "title": "Liver surgery when extrahepatic disease is present or treated",
     "question": "Does present or previously treated extrahepatic disease preclude liver cytoreduction or resection for well-differentiated NET liver metastases?",
     "kind": "clinical",
     "status": "Proposed · OPEN proposal",
     "where": [],
     "proposal": "Extrahepatic disease does not by itself preclude hepatic cytoreduction or resection of the primary for well-differentiated G1–G2 disease when at least 70% of liver disease can be removed or treated and accessible extrahepatic disease can be resected at the same time. Frame it as life-prolonging debulking; extrahepatic disease is associated with shorter survival in most, but not all, series (NANETS describes the data as conflicting).",
     "rules": [
      "Proceed when ≥70% debulking is achievable and accessible extrahepatic disease (mesenteric nodes, limited peritoneal deposits) can be removed; resect distant nodes only when this renders the patient free of visible disease.",
      "Bone metastases are an adverse modifier, not an automatic exclusion; diffuse skeletal, brain or unresectable mesenteric-root disease argue against surgery.",
      "No observation period is required before cytoreduction.",
      "Transplant questions go to NET-B4."

     "rationale": "NANETS consensus accepts extrahepatic disease for cytoreduction; cohorts show it shortens survival.",

       "says": "“5-year OS of at least 60%” The HCC trial-design source discusses a ≥60% five-year intention-to-treat benchmark. It is not a validated universal cross-cancer allocation rule and does not establish the proposed 5/10-patient monitoring counts.",

     "proposal": "Use a small staged pilot with all-screened accounting and explicit safety pauses; no automatic expansion on favorable recipient survival.",
     "rules": [
      "Proposed initial cap: ten transplants per separately approved biological stratum. Review after the first five have 90-day follow-up; no expansion decision until all first ten have at least 12-month follow-up. Reconcile vital status, graft events and known serious harms for every participant; require ≥90% completeness for other prespecified key outcomes.",
      "In an initial experimental cohort, one all-cause recipient death, graft loss or retransplantation within 90 days triggers a pause of further experimental enrollment/transplantation pending independent review. A later possibly treatment-related death/graft loss or a donor sentinel event also triggers review/pause. Rescue care is never withheld; reopening requires independent authorization.",
      "These are proposed conservative review triggers, not statistically validated efficacy/futility boundaries. Before opening, biostatistics and the independent board must ratify or replace them with indication-specific rules, denominators, pause authority and reopening criteria.",
      "Capture every screened candidate, including nonrecipients, conversion to resection, dropout, deaths and access barriers; report survival from entry and from LT, recurrence, graft use, donor recovery and quality of life. Ten survivors alone do not establish benefit or authorize expansion."

     "tests": "Locked eligibility strata; prospective entry/time-zero dataset; modern comparator; adverse-event definitions; follow-up-completeness report; independently signed statistical and safety plan.",
     "allocation": "Study monitoring never changes exception criteria or guarantees future access. Audit access by referral, geography, resources and donor availability without turning protected characteristics into exclusion rules.",
     "rationale": "A small pilot can test feasibility, staging fidelity, data capture and acute safety, not prove durable survival benefit. Define time zero, all-screened enrollment, waitlist failures, post-LT survival/recurrence, competing death, all grafts, donor harms and patient-reported outcomes before opening. An independent board needs actual pause/reopening authority.",
     "counter": "Zero observed events among ten fully followed independent patients still has a one-sided exact 95% binomial upper bound of 25.9% (1−0.05^(1/10)).      "certainty": "Strong methodological rationale for predefinition and ITT accounting; no empirical validation of our exact cap/interim/completeness thresholds. Late recurrence demands multi-year follow-up.",

{
 "key": "pdac",
 "code": "PDAC",
 "name": "Pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma",
 "generated": "29 October 2026",
 "files": {
  "roadmap_info": "PDAC_1_Roadmap.docx",
  "roadmap_questions": "PDAC_2_Roadmap_Questions.docx",
  "decision": "PDAC_7_Decision_Discussion.docx"
 },
 "sets": {
  "roadmap": {
   "label": "Roadmap",
   "page": "pdac/",
   "web": "pdac/#questions",
   "questions": [
    {
     "id": "PDAC-R1",
     "set": "roadmap",
     "title": "Surgery after oligometastatic disease responds",
     "question": "When synchronous oligometastatic PDAC responds to chemotherapy, or isolated lung metastases appear late, should surgery be offered outside a trial?",
     "kind": "clinical",
     "status": "Proposed; trial or registry first · OPEN proposal",
     "where": [],
     "proposal": "Distant metastasis stays systemic-therapy-led. Response-selected conversion surgery for limited liver metastases is offered preferably within a trial (METAPANC, CSPAC-1) or a registry after MDT review. Metachronous isolated lung metastases after a long disease-free interval may be resected. There is no PDAC transplant pathway.",
     "rules": [
      "Synchronous liver oligometastases: ≤3 liver metastases (OligoPanc working definition, relative-majority only; METAPANC ≤3 liver-only), no peritoneal or other extrahepatic disease, induction chemotherapy without progression (METAPANC: 8 cycles of mFOLFIRINOX; Heidelberg: usually ≥6 cycles with RECIST response of metastases and a marker fall), CA19-9 fall >50% to <500 U/mL (CSPAC-1), resectable primary and metastases.",
      "Counsel: in Heidelberg, 46% were unresectable at exploration and only about 1 in 4 explored was ypM0; median survival 25.5 months (ypM0) vs 10.7 (ypM1) vs 8.1 (exploration only). Surgery ≥9 months after diagnosis did worse.",
      "Metachronous isolated lung metastases: ≤3 (ideally solitary), unilateral, disease-free interval of about 2 years (17–28 months cited), after systemic therapy and MDT review.",
      "Para-aortic (16b1) nodes known before surgery are systemic disease and outside the OligoPanc Delphi definition (although panellists rated a para-aortic nodal vignette as oligometastatic); when found at operation, do not abort resection on 16b1 alone."
     ],
     "rationale": "Survival after resection is concentrated in complete responders, and unselected resection of metastases does not help. Trial rules give the clearest selection thresholds.",
     "studies": [
      {
       "source": "Hank 2022 · Heidelberg resection after chemotherapy",
       "key": "ehd-pdac_hank2022",
       "population": "Heidelberg, 173 explored after chemotherapy for metastatic PDAC. RECIST PR/CR of metastases plus a fall in CA19-9 and CEA, usually ≥6 cycles.",
       "results": "93 resected (45 ypM0); median survival 25.5 vs 10.7 vs 8.1 months; CA19-9 ≥400 HR 2.31; surgery ≥9 months after diagnosis HR 1.82.",
       "limits": "Single referral centre; no intention-to-treat denominator.",
       "locator": "Ann Surg 2022; Methods, Table 3.",
       "read": "Full text read"
      },
      {
       "source": "OligoPanc consensus (Leonhardt 2026)",
       "key": "ehd-pdac_oligopanc2026",

     "proposal": "Distant metastasis stays systemic-therapy-led.
